per_question.question: How does NC Medicaid define 'terminally ill' for purposes of hospice eligibility, and what certification is required?
per_question.agent_answer:
For NC Medicaid hospice, **“terminally ill” means the beneficiary has a life expectancy of six months or less**. The hospice policy’s certification and recertification provisions require the physician’s narrative and, for later benefit periods, expressly tie continued eligibility to whether the beneficiary **“continues to have a life expectancy of six months or less.”** [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment) (effective Mar. 15, 2024), § 5.4.1; D. *Certification and Recertification of Terminal Illness*. I did not find a more detailed standalone definition in the retrieved 3D text beyond that six-month life-expectancy standard.

## Required certification

NC Medicaid requires **written certification of terminal illness for each benefit period**. The hospice provider must obtain the written certification **before submitting a claim for payment**. If the written certification cannot be obtained within **two calendar days after a period begins**, an **oral certification must be obtained within two calendar days**, and the written certification must still be secured before the claim is submitted. Certifications may be completed **no more than 15 calendar days before** the effective date of election, and recertifications no more than **15 calendar days before** the next benefit period begins. [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment), §§ 5.4, 5.4.1.

## Who must sign it

For the **initial 90-day benefit period**, the hospice must obtain a written certification from:

- **the hospice medical director or the physician member of the hospice interdisciplinary group (IDG)**; and
- **the individual’s attending physician, if the individual has one**.

For **subsequent benefit periods**, only the **hospice medical director or physician member of the IDG** must certify. [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment), § 5.4.3.

## What the certification must contain

The certification or recertification must include:

- a **brief physician narrative** synthesizing the clinical information supporting the terminal diagnosis;
- the physician’s attestation that they composed the narrative after reviewing the clinical information and, where applicable, examining the beneficiary;
- a narrative reflecting the beneficiary’s **individual clinical circumstances**;
- the **election period dates** to which the certification applies; and
- the certifying or recertifying physician’s **signature and date**.

For the **third and later election periods**, the narrative must also explain why the **face-to-face encounter findings support a life expectancy of six months or less**. [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment), D. *Certification and Recertification of Terminal Illness*.

## Face-to-face requirement for later recertifications

Before the **third benefit period recertification and every recertification after that**, a **hospice physician or hospice nurse practitioner** must have a **face-to-face encounter** with the beneficiary. That encounter must occur **before, but no more than 30 calendar days before**, the recertification, to gather clinical findings for continued hospice eligibility. [Hospice Services](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3d-hospice-services/download?attachment), § 5.4.1.

If you want, I can also give you a one-paragraph version you could quote in an appeal or eligibility letter.
